Add datetime-related columns from BirdNET output filenames

Source: R/utils_column_editing.R
birdnet_add_datetime.Rd

Extracts and parses datetime information from filenames in the file path column (automatically detected), then adds several useful time-related columns (e.g., date, year, month, hour) to the input data frame. Several common formats are tried by default, and users can supply their own with formats (see Details).

Usage

birdnet_add_datetime(
  data,
  formats = c("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S", "%Y%m%d%H%M%S", "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S",
    "%Y%m%d_%H%M", "%d%m%Y_%H%M%S", "%m%d%Y_%H%M%S"),
  tz = "UTC",
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing BirdNET output.

formats

A character vector of datetime formats, using the same codes as strptime() (see Details). Formats are tried in order, and the first one that successfully parses a file name is used. Defaults to common year-first formats, plus day-first and month-first variants. See Details for how ambiguous dates are handled.

tz

A character string specifying the time zone to assign when parsing datetime. Defaults to "UTC".

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses the status messages about how many file names were parsed, failed, or were ambiguous. Warnings are still shown. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A data frame with additional columns:

datetime

POSIXct datetime parsed from the filename.

date

Date portion of the datetime.

year

Year of detection.

month

Month of detection.

mday

Day of the month.

yday

Day of the year.

hour

Hour of the day.

minute

Minute of the hour.

Rows whose file names can't be parsed get NA in all of these columns. Existing columns with these names are overwritten, with a warning. If all of these columns already exist, the data is returned unchanged.

Details

Defining your own formats. If the default formats don't match your file names, supply a format for each pattern in your data.

Supported codes:

  • %Y: 4-digit year (1900-2099)

  • %y: 2-digit year

  • %m: 2-digit month

  • %d: 2-digit day

  • %H, %M, %S: 2-digit hour, minute, second

Any other characters (such as _, -, or T) are matched literally. For example, site1_2024-06-15_0530.wav needs formats = "%Y-%m-%d_%H%M".

Ambiguous dates. The defaults include both day-first (%d%m%Y) and month-first (%m%d%Y) formats. A file name such as 05062023_133500 is valid as both, so the format listed first (day-first) is used and a message lists the rows to check. If your data uses only one convention, supply that format on its own to avoid the ambiguity.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
birdnet_add_datetime(example_jprf_2023) |>
glimpse()
} # }
